guide.title: How to Analyze a Migration Route
guide.sketch: Sketch a Route: Click the Draw Route Polyline button on the map to trace a route from an origin (e.g., Syria, Afghanistan, Libya) toward a European destination.
guide.analyze: Run Analysis: Click the Analyze Route button in the header.
guide.perspective: Take the Perspective of Refugees: Consider the documented obstacles and reflection questions to understand the challenges and uncertainties of forced displacement. Every journey to safety carries risks, regardless of the obstacles recorded here.
guide.purpose: Refugees fleeing persecution and war face information asymmetry: militarized border fences, pushbacks, maritime perils, and deportation camps are not clearly marked on ordinary maps. By simulating routes against unseen obstacles, students experience the daunting uncertainty faced by displaced persons.

guideModal.title: Refugee Migration Routes — Educational Guide
guideModal.perspectiveDescription: The purpose of this educational simulation is to allow students to step into the perspective of refugees and displaced persons escaping war, violence, human rights violations, or climate catastrophe in the Middle East, North Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, and Central Asia.
guideModal.invisibleHeading: Why Are Obstacles Invisible on the Map?
guideModal.invisibleDescription: In the real world, refugees do not possess perfect information. Militarized border fences, thermal surveillance cameras, violent pushback zones, and maritime interdiction zones are intentionally obscured or constantly shifting. Keeping the route-obstacles layer hidden in the map requires students to chart routes based on geography and assumption, just as displaced individuals must rely on informal networks, word-of-mouth, or human smugglers.
guideModal.centralMediterraneanDescription: Departs from Libya or Tunisia toward Lampedusa, Sicily, or Malta. Documented by the UN IOM as the deadliest maritime migration corridor in the world, with thousands of drownings, engine failures, and interceptions by Libyan coast guard forces leading to arbitrary detention.
guideModal.easternMediterraneanDescription: Passes through Turkey into Greece via the Aegean Sea islands (Lesvos, Samos, Chios) or across the Evros river border. Characterized by overloaded dinghies, dangerous currents, and pushbacks at sea.
guideModal.westernBalkanDescription: Traverses North Macedonia, Serbia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Hungary, and Croatia. Features double razor-wire border fences, police dog patrols, biometric surveillance, and extreme winter exposure in abandoned buildings.
guideModal.westernMediterraneanDescription: From Morocco or Algeria to mainland Spain, or from West Africa (Senegal, Mauritania) across open ocean to the Canary Islands. The Atlantic route involves open wooden pirogues facing weeks of treacherous currents.
guideModal.discussionQuestion1: Why do refugees choose dangerous irregular routes instead of boarding a plane or taking a ferry? (Lack of legal visas and airline carrier sanctions).
guideModal.discussionQuestion2: When European nations fortify one border (e.g. Hungarian border fence in 2015), how does the migratory flow shift toward more hazardous mountain or maritime passages?
guideModal.discussionQuestion3: What responsibilities do states have under the 1951 Geneva Refugee Convention regarding non-refoulement (the principle of not forcing refugees to return to a country where they face persecution)?

descriptions.minimal: No significant documented obstacles were encountered within the route corridor. Note that unexpected checkpoints or shifting border controls may still occur.
descriptions.low: Relatively low concentration of major documented obstacles, though refugees still face physical exhaustion, precarious legal status, and unexpected border changes.
descriptions.moderate: Significant barriers encountered. Journeys along this corridor present hazardous terrain, active border interdictions, or risky transit conditions requiring dangerous detours.
descriptions.high: Severe perils present. Multiple life-threatening hazards (open sea, militarized borders, or desert corridors) with documented humanitarian crises and human rights violations.
descriptions.critical: Extreme, multi-tiered danger. This corridor traverses several of the deadliest checkpoints and crossing points on migration journeys into Europe, with very high risks of fatality, violence, or prolonged detention.

narratives.maritime: Maritime Crossing Reality: Sea crossings involve unseaworthy vessels, no life vests, hypothermia, and fear of capsizing in darkness. Refugees often pay their life savings for a spot on a dinghy without knowing if rescue ships are allowed to dock.
narratives.border: Border Wall & Pushback Reality: Militarized border fences with razor wire, thermal cameras, and armed patrols mean refugees must repeatedly attempt crossings ('The Game'), facing violent pushbacks, confiscated phones, and physical injuries.
narratives.terrain: Harsh Environmental Reality: Crossing freezing mountain passes or blistering deserts on foot without adequate shoes, water, or shelter leads to frostbite, trench foot, severe dehydration, and exhaustion.
narratives.detention: Human Rights & Vulnerability Reality: Without safe, legal escape routes, refugees are vulnerable to human trafficking, arbitrary detention in squalid camps, and extortion by organized criminal networks.
narratives.general: Every journey across borders without legal documentation carries psychological stress, fear of apprehension, separation from family members, and reliance on unpredictable conditions.

obstaclePerspectives.obs-med-central: Imagine being packed with 120 people on a deflating rubber raft in 3-meter waves at midnight, with engine fumes making passengers vomit and no rescue vessel in sight.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-med-libya-coast: Being pulled back means losing all savings, returning to arbitrary captivity in detention centers, and starting the trauma all over again.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-sahara-desert: Thousands die undocumented in the desert sands before ever seeing the sea. Water runs out in hours if a vehicle breaks down.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-aegean-crossing: Fearing detection by thermal cameras, smugglers force passengers to jump into cold deep water meters away from rocky cliffs in darkness.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-evros-border: Refugees report being stripped of phones, money, and warm clothes before being forced back across the frigid river.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-balkan-mountains: Refugees sleep outdoors in makeshift tents with plastic tarps in freezing snow, suffering severe trench foot, frostbite, and animal attacks.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-hungary-fence: Fences do not stop people fleeing war; they only force them into the hands of organized smugglers who charge thousands of euros for dangerous hidden compartments.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-drina-river: Refugees must swim across fast-flowing winter water with all their belongings in plastic bags tied around their necks.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-smuggler-extortion: Refugees are often trapped with no legal recourse, completely at the mercy of criminal networks because safe legal pathways do not exist.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-alps-winter: Walking for 8 hours through waist-deep snow in worn-out sneakers to reach safety, risking amputation from severe frostbite.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-channel-straits: Tiny inflatable boats dodge massive 400-meter container ships whose wash can overturn small craft in seconds.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-water-scarcity: Diabetic children and elderly grandmothers must walk dozens of kilometers daily without basic medicines or clean water.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-western-balkans-camp: Months spent in bureaucratic limbo, trapped in mud and cold, waiting for a chance to attempt 'The Game' (crossing borders) again.
obstaclePerspectives.obs-morocco-melilla: Desperate collective attempts to scale the fences have resulted in dozens of deaths and severe crush injuries.

reflectionQuestions.1: Why might a family fleeing conflict feel they have no choice but to take this dangerous route?
reflectionQuestions.2: How does the lack of safe and legal asylum pathways affect the decisions refugees must make?
reflectionQuestions.3: If one border or maritime corridor is heavily blocked, where do you think refugee flows divert?
reflectionQuestions.4: What psychological and physical toll would encountering these obstacles take on a person or child?
